##Mutate and plotr
```{r}
cp <- cp %>%
  dplyr::select(any_of(c("bmd", "name", "bmdl", "bmdu", "exp_name", "is_sqrt"))) %>%
  mutate(source = "CP") %>%
  rename(exp = exp_name) %>%
  mutate(
    name = ifelse(name == "Taxol (Paclitaxel)", "Taxol", name),
    name = ifelse(name == "Berberine Chloride", "Berberine chloride", name)
  )

shape_list <- c("rep1" =16, "rep2" =17, "rep3" =18, "rep4" =1)
plot <- ggplot(cp, aes(x = bmd, y = name, colour = is_sqrt, shape = exp)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = bmdl, xmax = bmdu), width = 0.2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_shape_manual(name = "exp", values = shape_list) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13, margin = margin(t = 15)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, colour = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6, colour = "black", margin = margin(r = 5)),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1)
  )

plot
ggsave("../Plots/sqrt_bmd_results.png", plot, width = 15, height = 10,units = "cm")
```

#Load data
```{r}
# Load tcplfit results from a given rep's folder. Written as a self-contained
# function (rather than reassigning a shared `tcpl_results_folder` variable
# before each rep's `list.files()` call) so a stray edit or out-of-order
# chunk execution can't silently pull one rep's data from another rep's
# folder (or a non-folder path).
load_tcpl_folder <- function(folder) {
  list.files(folder, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE) |>
    map_dfr(function(path) {
      label <- basename(path) |>
        str_remove("^tcpl_results") |>
        str_remove("\\.csv$")

      read.csv(path) |>
        mutate(
          low_variance    = str_detect(label, "lowvar"),
          pearson_thresh  = str_extract(label, "(?<=pearson_)[0-9.]+") |> as.numeric(),
          commonfeature = str_detect(label, "common"),
          removedfeatures = str_detect(label, "removed"),
          source_file    = basename(path),
          source_folder   = folder
        )
    })
}
rep1 <- load_tcpl_folder("../Output/rep1/tcplfit_results/")
rep2 <- load_tcpl_folder("../Output/rep2/tcplfit_results/")
rep3 <- load_tcpl_folder("../Output/rep3/tcplfit_results/")
rep4 <- load_tcpl_folder("../Output/rep4/tcplfit_results/")

joined <- rbind(rep1, rep2, rep3, rep4) %>%
  dplyr::filter(source_file != "tcpl_results_pearson_none.csv")%>% # same as _all_features, so removing one
  mutate(
    name = ifelse(name == "Taxol (Paclitaxel)", "Taxol", name),
    name = ifelse(name == "Berberine Chloride", "Berberine chloride", name)
  )%>%
  rename(exp = exp_name)
```

##plot pearsons
```{r}

all_results <- joined %>%
  dplyr::select(any_of(c("bmd", "name", "bmdl", "bmdu", "exp", "pearson_thresh", "low_variance", "removedfeatures"))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!low_variance) %>% #get rid of low varience est info'
   dplyr::filter(removedfeatures == FALSE)  #remove removed features

plot <- ggplot(all_results, aes(x = bmd, y = name, colour = pearson_thresh)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = bmdl, xmax = bmdu), width = 0.2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(na.value = "red") +
  theme_bw() +
  facet_wrap(~exp)+
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13, margin = margin(t = 15)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, colour = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6, colour = "black", margin = margin(r = 5)),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1)
  )

plot

# Average across reps (exp) within each chemical / pearson_thresh cutoff, so
# each name x pearson_thresh combo collapses to a single point.
all_results_avg <- all_results %>%
  group_by(name, pearson_thresh) %>%
  summarise(
    n_reps = sum(!is.na(bmd)),
    bmd = mean(bmd, na.rm = TRUE),
    bmdl = mean(bmdl, na.rm = TRUE),
    bmdu = mean(bmdu, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # mean() of all-NA groups yields NaN; keep these as NA
  mutate(across(c(bmd, bmdl, bmdu), ~ ifelse(is.nan(.x), NA, .x)))

plot <- ggplot(all_results_avg, aes(x = bmd, y = name, colour = pearson_thresh)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = bmdl, xmax = bmdu), width = 0.2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(na.value = "red") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13, margin = margin(t = 15)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, colour = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6, colour = "black", margin = margin(r = 5)),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1)
  )

plot


# --- 1. CI width per threshold (log scale, since bmd is log-distributed) ---
ci_width_summary <- all_results %>%
  filter(!is.na(bmd), !is.na(bmdl), !is.na(bmdu)) %>%
  mutate(log_ci_width = log10(bmdu) - log10(bmdl)) %>%
  group_by(pearson_thresh) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_log_ci_width   = mean(log_ci_width, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_log_ci_width = median(log_ci_width, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_fits = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ci_width_summary

# --- 2. Fit success rate per threshold ---
fit_rate_summary <- all_results %>%
  group_by(pearson_thresh) %>%
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    n_valid_bmd = sum(!is.na(bmd)),
    fit_rate_pct = n_valid_bmd / n_total * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

fit_rate_summary

# --- 3. Cross-replicate reproducibility per threshold ---
# For each chemical x threshold, how consistent is bmd across reps (exp)?
# Use coefficient of variation (CV) on the log scale — robust to BMD's wide dynamic range
reproducibility_summary <- all_results %>%
  filter(!is.na(bmd)) %>%
  group_by(name, pearson_thresh) %>%
  summarise(
    n_reps = n(),
    log_bmd_sd = sd(log10(bmd), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_reps >= 2) %>%   # CV only meaningful with 2+ reps present
  group_by(pearson_thresh) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_log_bmd_sd = mean(log_bmd_sd, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_chemicals_compared = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

reproducibility_summary

# --- Combine all three into one comparison table ---
threshold_comparison <- ci_width_summary %>%
  left_join(fit_rate_summary, by = "pearson_thresh") %>%
  left_join(reproducibility_summary, by = "pearson_thresh") %>%
  arrange(pearson_thresh)

threshold_comparison

#PLOT

threshold_comparison %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(mean_log_ci_width, fit_rate_pct, mean_log_bmd_sd),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pearson_thresh, y = value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Pearson correlation threshold", y = NULL,
       title = "BMD modeling quality across correlation thresholds")
```

# Pearson analysis 0.9 pie charts
```{r}
# List of replicate folders — update paths/names as needed
rep_dirs <- c(
  rep1 = "../Output/rep1",
  rep2 = "../Output/rep2",
  rep3 = "../Output/rep3"
)

rep_files <- file.path(rep_dirs, "test_chem_well_pearson_0.9.csv")
names(rep_files) <- names(rep_dirs)

# Read each file and extract the set of retained feature names (non-metadata)
retained_features <- imap(rep_files, function(path, rep_name) {
  df <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  feature_cols <- names(df)[!str_detect(names(df), "^Metadata_")]
  feature_cols
})

# Fit and plot the Euler diagram
fit <- euler(retained_features)

plot(fit,
     quantities = TRUE,
     fills = list(fill = c("#66C2A5", "#FC8D62", "#8DA0CB"), alpha = 0.6),
     labels = list(font = 2),
     main = "Overlap of features retained after 0.9 Pearson filter")

# --- Subset each rep down to the features common to all three ---

# Intersection of feature names across all three reps
common_features <- reduce(retained_features, intersect)
length(common_features)  # should be 183

# Re-read each rep's full retained file (rows + all its own retained columns),
# then subset to metadata + the common feature set
rep_common <- imap(rep_files, function(path, rep_name) {
  df <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  meta_cols <- names(df)[str_detect(names(df), "^Metadata_")]
  df %>% dplyr::select(all_of(meta_cols), all_of(common_features))
})

# Write out the subsetted files, one per rep, into their own folders
iwalk(rep_common, function(df, rep_name) {
  write_csv(df, file.path(rep_dirs[[rep_name]], "test_chem_well_pearson_0.9_common.csv"))
})


feature_breakdown <- tibble(feature = common_features) %>%
  mutate(
    module = str_extract(feature, "^[^_]+"),
    region = str_extract(feature, "(cells|cytoplasm|nuclei)$"),
    channel1 = case_when(
      module == "Correlation" ~
        str_match(feature,
          "^Correlation_[^_]+_(AGP|ER|DNA|Mito|RNA)_(AGP|ER|DNA|Mito|RNA)_"
        )[, 2],
      TRUE ~ str_extract(feature, "_(AGP|ER|DNA|Mito|RNA)(_|$)") %>%
               str_remove_all("_")
    ),
    channel2 = case_when(
      module == "Correlation" ~
        str_match(feature,
          "^Correlation_[^_]+_(AGP|ER|DNA|Mito|RNA)_(AGP|ER|DNA|Mito|RNA)_"
        )[, 3],
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(module, region, channel1, channel2), as.character))

#deal why the multiple channels
feature_breakdown <- feature_breakdown %>%
  mutate(
    channel_pair = if_else(
      !is.na(channel2),
      paste(pmin(channel1, channel2), pmax(channel1, channel2), sep = "-"),  # order-independent, so DNA-Mito == Mito-DNA
      channel1
    )
  )


make_pie <- function(df, group_col, title) {
  counts <- df %>%
    dplyr::count(.data[[group_col]], name = "n") %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[group_col]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100)

  ggplot(counts, aes(x = "", y = n, fill = .data[[group_col]])) +
    geom_col(width = 1, color = "white") +
    coord_polar(theta = "y") +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, " (", round(pct, 1), "%)")),
              position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3) +
    labs(title = title, fill = group_col) +
    theme_void()
}

# 1. Distribution by module (e.g., AreaShape, Intensity, Texture, Correlation, Granularity, RadialDistribution)
p_module <- make_pie(feature_breakdown, "module",
                      "Feature module distribution (common features, 0.9 Pearson filter)")
p_module

# 2. Distribution by region (cells / cytoplasm / nuclei)
p_region <- make_pie(feature_breakdown, "region",
                      "Feature region distribution (common features)")
p_region

# 3. Distribution by channel1 (primary channel: AGP, ER, DNA, Mito, RNA)
p_channel1 <- make_pie(feature_breakdown, "channel1",
                        "Feature channel distribution (common features)")
p_channel1

p_channel_pair <- make_pie(feature_breakdown, "channel_pair",
                            "Feature channel distribution (common features)")

p_channel_pair

#checking the totals
check_total <- function(df, group_col) {
  df %>%
    dplyr::count(.data[[group_col]], name = "n") %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      total_n = sum(n),
      total_incl_na = sum(n),
      total_excl_na = sum(n[!is.na(.data[[group_col]])])
    )
}

check_total(feature_breakdown, "module")
check_total(feature_breakdown, "region")

#not every features has a dye
check_total(feature_breakdown, "channel1")

#not every features has a dye
check_total(feature_breakdown, "channel_pair")
module_counts_09 <- feature_breakdown %>%
  dplyr::count(module, name = "n_after") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pct_after = n_after / sum(n_after) * 100)

```

```{r}
          "^Correlation_[^_]+_(AGP|ER|DNA|Mito|RNA)_(AGP|ER|DNA|Mito|RNA)_"
        )[, 3],
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(module, region, channel1, channel2), as.character))

#deal why the multiple channels
feature_breakdown <- feature_breakdown %>%
  mutate(
    channel_pair = if_else(
      !is.na(channel2),
      paste(pmin(channel1, channel2), pmax(channel1, channel2), sep = "-"),  # order-independent, so DNA-Mito == Mito-DNA
      channel1
    )
  )


make_pie <- function(df, group_col, title) {
  counts <- df %>%
    dplyr::count(.data[[group_col]], name = "n") %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[group_col]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100)

  ggplot(counts, aes(x = "", y = n, fill = .data[[group_col]])) +
    geom_col(width = 1, color = "white") +
    coord_polar(theta = "y") +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, " (", round(pct, 1), "%)")),
              position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3) +
    labs(title = title, fill = group_col) +
    theme_void()
}

# 1. Distribution by module (e.g., AreaShape, Intensity, Texture, Correlation, Granularity, RadialDistribution)
p_module <- make_pie(feature_breakdown, "module",
                      "Feature module distribution (183 common features, 0.9 Pearson filter)")
p_module

# 2. Distribution by region (cells / cytoplasm / nuclei)
p_region <- make_pie(feature_breakdown, "region",
                      "Feature region distribution (183 common features)")
p_region

# 3. Distribution by channel1 (primary channel: AGP, ER, DNA, Mito, RNA)
p_channel1 <- make_pie(feature_breakdown, "channel1",
                        "Feature channel distribution (183 common features)")
p_channel1

p_channel_pair <- make_pie(feature_breakdown, "channel_pair",
                            "Feature channel distribution (183 common features)")

p_channel_pair

#checking the totals
check_total <- function(df, group_col) {
  df %>%
    dplyr::count(.data[[group_col]], name = "n") %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      total_n = sum(n),
      total_incl_na = sum(n),
      total_excl_na = sum(n[!is.na(.data[[group_col]])])
    )
}

check_total(feature_breakdown, "module")

check_total(feature_breakdown, "region")

#not every features has a dye
check_total(feature_breakdown, "channel1")

#not every features has a dye
check_total(feature_breakdown, "channel_pair")
module_counts_none <- feature_breakdown %>%
  dplyr::count(module, name = "n_before") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pct_before = n_before / sum(n_before) * 100)
```

##Retention
```{r}
module_retention <- module_counts_none %>%
  dplyr::full_join(module_counts_09, by = "module") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_before   = tidyr::replace_na(n_before, 0),
    n_after    = tidyr::replace_na(n_after, 0),
    pct_before = tidyr::replace_na(pct_before, 0),
    pct_after  = tidyr::replace_na(pct_after, 0),
    retention_rate = ifelse(n_before > 0, n_after / n_before * 100, NA_real_),
    share_change   = pct_after - pct_before   # change in composition share, not retention
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n_before))

module_retention
```
